llm_findings: Single causal change: --ngram-ve-dim 64 changes table width from 128 to 64, including the necessarily dimension-dependent up-projections. train.py lines 715–730 and 5909–5924 document this independent width option; no second configuration change is proposed.

Repository evidence supports the experiment: pinned controls report 592.9M parameters with four 1048576×128 tables, while the no-ngram smoke reports 55.7M parameters, 410 versus 334 same-host steps, and BPB 1.173413 versus 1.165855. Halving table width predicts approximately 324M parameters, consistent with the exercise check.

The supplied decision log contains no closed table-width direction. The discarded --ngram-rms-fp32 experiment changes precision, and the no-ngram smoke removes the feature entirely; neither duplicates retaining four tables at width 64.
Competition-legal scope: README.md permits model-size and architecture changes. This flag introduces no pretrained weights, external data, tokenizer changes, or evaluator changes.

The expected effect is falsifiable through the controller-pinned seed-42, full-chip, 1800-second matched comparison: +6–12% steps and a 0.001–0.004 public-BPB reduction are measurable predictions, with explicit success and capacity-loss criteria.

Evidence limitations are non-blocking: parameter count and removal throughput do not prove which traffic component dominates, and the BF16-SDPA win does not establish that width reduction will improve quality. The no-ngram result is smoke-only, so it cannot bracket full-budget BPB; the declared matched full-run criterion, rather than that interpolation, should determine the outcome.
